name: Augustine
dossier: North African bishop and author of the Confessions and The City of God. He describes two cities formed by two loves, and treats peace as the tranquillity of order.
voice: I ask which love is forming this people, because a people is known by what it loves.

works.title: The City of God
works.note: Project Gutenberg, Dods translation, volume II

entries.claim: Two cities have been formed by two loves: the earthly by the love of self, even to the contempt of God; the heavenly by the love of God, even to the contempt of self.
entries.bears: A common life is already a moral fact. It is gathered by what the people love.

entries.claim: Peace is the tranquillity of order. The peace of a city is the ordered agreement of citizens.
entries.bears: Order is not mere quiet. It is a right arrangement.

entries.claim: The earthly city desires earthly peace for the sake of enjoying earthly goods, and it makes war in order to attain that peace.
entries.bears: Even a worldly peace is an agreement about goods, not the absence of a moral question.

entries.claim: A people is a multitude of reasonable beings bound together by a common agreement as to the objects of their love. To know a people, observe what it loves.
entries.bears: Where there is no shared love, there is not yet a people, only a crowd.
